correctness.rationale: Read original printed equation (5.2) and Hamiltonian/costates (5.3) from the actual publisher PDF page 8. Differentiation w.r.t S gives −∂H/∂S=λ1(aE+v)−λ2 aE, a=(1−u2)θ(I),v=µ+z0u1; print has −λ2(aE+v), introducing −vλ2. Independently expanded all three Hamiltonian gradients by symbolic differentiation (SymPy), which agrees with source for costates 2 and 3 but not costate 1. With terminal λ3=λ2=λ1=0 and positive infection penalty C3, λ3(T−τ)=C3τ+..., hence λ2(T−τ)=α C3 τ²/2+...; since v≥µ>0, the source discrepancy is nonzero near T, not algebraically equivalent. This diagnoses necessary conditions, not actual implementation or displayed numerical trajectories.

value.rationale: A printed necessary condition in a concrete published optimal-control epidemic model has an active sign/variable error, changing the backward boundary-value system and therefore the mathematical basis for reported optimal interventions. Identifying and correcting that specific inconsistency with a nonvanishing terminal witness is useful even though differentiation itself is elementary.

final_claim: In Witbooi–Vyambwera–Nsuami (2023) vaccinated three-state SEIR Pontryagin system, the published first adjoint has spurious −(µ+z0u1)λ2; actual −∂H/∂S equals λ1[(1−u2)θ(I)E+µ+z0u1]−λ2(1−u2)θ(I)E. Under stated positive parameters and terminal zero adjoints, λ2(T−τ)=α C3 τ²/2+O(τ³), so the printed and correct backward systems differ nontrivially near terminal time.
